title: Single Cell RNA Sequencing (scRNA-seq)
author: Edgar Otto
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7dthi6n
materials: Gently pipette mix with Wide Bore pipette tip
Place the Chip in the Holder before loading reagents
After loading Master Mix, wait for 00:00:30
Then, immediately proceed to loading the Gel Beads
Fold and lock Chip Holder at 45° angle
Cycle in Bio-Rad C1000 TouchTM thermal cycler with Deep Well Module

steps.title: Thaw Biopsy
steps.instruction: Remove biopsy frozen in 500 µL CryoStor solution (1.8 mL cryovial) from liquid nitrogen. Thaw in a 37 °C water bath with constant swirling for 60-90 sec until the biopsy is ice-free.

steps.title: Wash Biopsy
steps.instruction: Perform a two-step wash of the biopsy at room temperature using DMEM/F12/10%FBS.

substeps.instruction: Transfer biopsy to a 3.5 cm plastic petri dish with 1 ml DMEM/F12/10%FBS for 10 seconds to wash off DMSO.
Transfer to a second 3.5 cm plastic petri dish with 1 ml DMEM/F12/10%FBS and incubate for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Biopsy for Dissociation
steps.instruction: Document and size the biopsy tissue.

substeps.instruction: Take a picture of the biopsy next to a ruler.
Cut biopsy into ~1 mm pieces using a scalpel.

steps.title: Prepare Dissociation Medium
steps.instruction: Prepare the dissociation medium in a noBind 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

substeps.instruction: Combine 450 µL DMEM/F12 (no FBS) and 50 µL Liberase TL (stock conc.: 2.5 mg/ml H2O; final enzyme conc.: 0.25 mg/ml).

steps.title: Dissociate Tissue
steps.instruction: Perform enzymatic dissociation of the biopsy tissue at 37 °C.

substeps.instruction: Transfer biopsy tissue to the dissociation medium prewarmed to 37 °C.
Incubate at 37 °C for 12 minutes while shaking at 500 rpm in an Eppendorf Thermomixer.
Triturate 15 times with a wide bore 1 mL pipette tip after the first 6 minutes of incubation.

steps.title: Stop Reaction and Filter
steps.instruction: Stop the enzymatic reaction and filter the suspension to remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Stop the reaction by adding 500 µL DMEM/F12/10%FBS (room temperature) and gently mixing.
Incubate for 1 minute at room temperature.
Filter through a 30 µm gaze (Miltenyi) into a 15 mL tube on ice, pushing tissue through with a 5 mL syringe plunger (rubber side).
Wash the filter with 10 mL cold DMEM/F12/10%FBS.
Filter the suspension again through a new 30 µm gaze (Miltenyi) into a second 15 mL tube.
Wash the first 15 mL tube with 1 mL cold DMEM/F12/10% FBS and apply through the 30 µm gaze into the second 15 mL tube.

steps.title: Concentrate and Count Cells
steps.instruction: Concentrate the cell suspension and determine viable cell count.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the suspension at 200 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Remove supernatant using a glass Pasteur pipette and house vacuum (leaving ~20 µL).
Carefully add and dispense 40 µL DMEM/F12/10%FBS to the cell pellet.
Take 5 µL of the suspension and mix with 5 µL Trypan blue.
Count viable cells using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter (Countess).

steps.title: Load Cells to Chromium Array
steps.instruction: Load the prepared cells into the 10X Chromium array ASAP.

substeps.instruction: Load up to 10,000 viable cells in up to 46 µL of cell suspension.

steps.title: Alternative Biopsy Cryopreservation
steps.instruction: Follow these steps for immediate cryopreservation of renal biopsy specimens.

substeps.instruction: Place a 1.8 mL cryovial with 1.5 mL HypoThermosol on ice and add the renal biopsy specimen immediately.
Keep upright at 4 °C (on ice) until cryopreservation.
Place a 1.8 mL cryovial with 1.5 mL CryoStor CS10 on ice and transfer the specimen very quickly.
Keep upright on ice for 15 minutes for permeabilization.
Place the cryovial in a Mr. Frosty freezing unit containing isopropanol and store in a -80 °C freezer for 24 hours.
Transfer the cryovial to submerged liquid N2.

steps.title: Wash and Resuspend Cells
steps.instruction: Clean the cell suspension to remove contaminants and ambient RNA.

substeps.instruction: Transfer cells in media to a 2 mL Eppendorf tube and spin down to form a pellet.
Remove supernatant and gently add 1x PBS + 0.04% BSA away from the pellet.
Repeat the wash one more time and spin down again.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 1x PBS + 0.04% BSA with gentle pipette mixing (do not invert tubes).
Adjust to the desired cell concentration.

steps.title: Prepare 10X Chromium Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the reagents and hardware for the 10X run.

substeps.instruction: Equilibrate Single Cell 3’ Gel Beads to room temperature for at least 30 minutes and thaw reagents.
Resuspend RT primer in 40 µL low TE buffer and prepare the thermal cycler.
Prepare Master Mix on ice (do not add cells yet).
Insert the chip into the holder by aligning beveled corners at the upper left, pressing the right side until the clip engages, and closing the holder flat on the benchtop.

steps.title: Prepare Cell-Master Mix
steps.instruction: Combine the cell suspension with the Master Mix on a chilled metal block on ice.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 66.2 µL Master Mix into each well of an 8-tube strip and add the calculated volume of water.
Estimate cell suspension volume and set pipette to half that volume for mixing.
Pipette the required volume of cell suspension from the center of the suspension.
Add the cell suspension to the tube strip containing Master Mix.
Gently mix 5 times with a pipette set to 90 µL.
Transfer 90 µL of the mixture to the wells in row 1 of the chip, avoiding bubbles.

steps.title: Load Gel Beads and Oil
steps.instruction: Load the Gel Beads and Partitioning Oil into the chip.

substeps.instruction: Vortex the Single Cell 3’ Gel Bead Strip in a 10x Vortex Adapter for 30 seconds.
Flick the strip in a sharp downward motion to ensure maximum recovery.
Pipette 40 µL Gel Beads into the bottom of the wells in row 2, avoiding bubbles.
Transfer Partitioning Oil to a reservoir and load row 3; run the chip within 2 minutes of adding oil.

steps.title: Run Chromium Controller
steps.instruction: Seal the chip and execute the run.

substeps.instruction: Attach the 10X Gasket (notch at top left), ensuring holes align with wells and the assembly remains horizontal.
Load the assembled Chip, Holder, and Gasket into the instrument.
Confirm the Chromium Single Cell A program and start the run (approx. 6 minutes 30 seconds).

steps.title: Recover GEMs
steps.instruction: Collect the GEMs from the chip into a PCR plate.

substeps.instruction: Remove the chip from the controller and open the holder to a 45-degree angle.
Remove the gasket.
Aspirate 100 µL GEMs from the recovery well within 2 minutes of the run completion.
Dispense GEMs slowly (20 sec) into a twin.tec® 96-Well PCR plate on a chilled block, pipetting against the side of the well.
Seal the plate with a Bio-Rad PX1™ Plate Sealer (red stripe up).
Store at 4 °C for up to 72 hours.

steps.title: Post-GEM Recovery
steps.instruction: Recover the cDNA from the GEMs.

substeps.instruction: Add 125 µL Recovery Agent directly to samples in the PCR plate.
Move the entire volume to 8-tube strips without vortexing or pipette mixing.
Slowly remove 125 µL of the pink Recovery Agent/Partitioning Oil layer from the bottom and discard.

steps.title: cDNA Amplification and Sequencing
steps.instruction: Amplify the cDNA and perform library preparation for sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Set up cDNA Amplification Master Mix and perform amplification.
Perform Bioanalyzer QC (optimal mean length > 2 kb).
Sequence the library on an Illumina HiSeq 4000 platform.
